manifest.purpose: The correct answer file mirroring submission/trojan_report.json exactly. Top-level fields: trojan_detected=true, suspect_instances=[one object], summary (string >=20 chars). The single suspect_instances entry has instance_name='u_grant_ff' (exact identifier from access_ctrl_netlist.v line instantiating DFF_NEGEDGE), cell_type='DFF_NEGEDGE', sampled_signal='grant_pre' (exact net name driving .d port of u_grant_ff, declared as 'wire grant_pre' and produced by u_and_final AND2 gate), and justification (free text, >=1 sentence) explaining that design_brief.md mandates all state elements use DFF_POSEDGE per the documented clocking discipline, but u_grant_ff is instantiated as DFF_NEGEDGE, causing it to sample grant_pre on the falling edge of clk instead of the rising edge like every other pipeline register (u_req_ff, u_key_reg0-7, u_cmp_ff, u_out_ff), creating a half-cycle timing window where a stale/transitional value of the access-permission comparator output can propagate to grant_out. Summary field restates: single DFF_NEGEDGE substitution found on u_grant_ff instance sampling grant_pre, violating the single posedge clocking discipline documented in design_brief.md. This file satisfies FR1-FR4 (valid JSON, correct field types, non-empty required strings referencing verbatim netlist identifiers, internal consistency between trojan_detected=true and non-empty suspect_instances) and SR1-SR4 (correct instance name, correct cell_type, correct sampled_signal, trojan_detected=true). No other file changes are needed since this is a report-grading domain; inputs/ files remain untouched and are not re-emitted.
